articles.title: Predicting AEW All In 2026 Surprises From Britt Baker's Return to New Day's Debut
articles.summary: All In has been AEW's premier pay-per-view event since its inception in 2023, and the upcoming installment has the potential to be equally exceptional with what's on tap.
articles.body:
All In has been AEW's premier pay-per-view event since its inception in 2023, and the upcoming installment has the potential to be equally exceptional with what's on tap.

Kenny Omega and Will Ospreay's highly anticipated main event, Willow Nightingale and Mercedes Moné's AEW Women's World Championship clash and the first-time encounter over the AEW World Tag Team Championship are all guaranteed to be great from an in-ring standpoint, but there are bound to be several surprises in store as well.

All In 2024 featured Nigel McGuinness' return to the ring in his native England and Ricochet's All Elite Wrestling debut, while the returns of Bryan Danielson and Darby Allin highlighted All In 2025, so a precedent has been set for milestone moments occurring at the annual event.

From unpredictable outcomes to new champions being crowned, these are six shockers that could feasibly transpire at All In 2026.

Britt Baker Returns in Women's Casino Gauntlet

It was at All In two years ago that Britt Baker, an AEW original, had her last major match in the promotion, unsuccessfully challenging Mercedes Moné for the AEW TBS Championship.

However, the battle between two of the bigger names in women's wrestling in the last decade fell well short of fans' expectations.

Baker only made a handful of appearances on AEW TV after that before disappearing entirely from programming in November 2024. Although Tony Khan has responded to inquiries regarding her absence on media conference calls since then, her status hasn't seemed to change.

Baker was brought back up again by fans recently when Fightful Select 's Sean Ross Sapp revealed in a Q&A that she was internally discussed for the upcoming Rebel tribute edition of Dynamite on Sept. 9 in Georgia. The two were synonymous with each other in AEW's first few years.

It would make sense to reintroduce her before then in the women's Casino Gauntlet match at All In, where the winner will earn a future shot at the AEW Women's World Championship she once held.

The wrestling dentist doesn't necessarily have to win, but it would be quite the surprise to see her again amid social media rumors that she's eyeing an exit from the company due to her inactivity.

Kevin Knight is scheduled to have his biggest bout yet at All In when he defends the AEW TNT Championship against Darby Allin in a Falls Count Anywhere match.

The reigning champ is in the middle of a career year, having held the title since early April and racking up the most successful defenses for the TNT title ever. He also headlined last month's Redemption event with AEW world champion Kenny Omega and looked credible in defeat.

He's been a member of The Don Callis Family since shortly after turning heel at Double or Nothing in May, the same show where he betrayed his buddy, Darby Allin. Seeds have been planted over the last month that this new sinister side of Knight isn't the real him and that he'll soon see the light once he's away from Callis.

Perhaps it's his obsession with the gold that has made him so arrogant, and once he loses it to Allin on AEW's biggest stage, he'll realize the error of his ways.

While such a significant development for his character would be premature at this stage, it isn't completely out of the question for Sunday's pay-per-view.

Nigel McGuinness Wins the AEW Continental Championship

The ongoing Continental Challenge Cup has been a unique way of determining what the AEW Continental Championship match will be at All In, and as of this writing, only four wrestlers remain.

It will be either Jon Moxley or Claudio Castagnoli taking on Kyle O'Reilly or Nigel McGuinness for the title.

As the defending champ, Moxley should walk into the event with the belt, and seeing as how he already beat O'Reilly to retain the title in May, the finals of the tournament should be Moxley vs. McGuinness at All In.

In such a situation, Moxley would be automatically expected to emerge victorious, which would make an upset from McGuinness all the more surprising.

As noted, it was at All In two years ago that he returned to the ring for the first time since 2011 in front of his countrymen at Wembley Stadium. It would be huge for him to be the one to end Moxley's lengthy title reign on that same show two years later.

McGuinness may not be a full-time member of the active roster anymore, but it would be a fitting final chapter to his career as well as a memorable moment for those in attendance.

The New Day Win the AEW World Trios Titles with Swerve Strickland

Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods have been a hot topic of conversation among wrestling fans since receiving their release from WWE at the beginning of May.

They were always expected to have interest from AEW upon entering free agency, and now their debut may be imminent.

Swerve Strickland curiously teased challenging for the AEW World Trios Championship on a recent Dynamite. Since he doesn't currently have any established allies on the roster, it was safe for fans to assume that he could be enlisting the likes of the former New Day to go after the gold with him.

Kingston and Woods obviously belong in the tag team ranks, but there's nothing wrong with starting them out with Strickland to ensure them a spot on the show. Plus, Strickland and The New Day could turn out to be quite the formidable force.

The AEW World Trios title match for All In is not yet set in stone, but if it's some sort of multi-team affair featuring a variety of trios, look for Strickland and New Day to not only enter but also to leave as the new champions.

Willow Nightingale and Mercedes Moné are no strangers to each other. They've collided in both New Japan Pro-Wrestling and in AEW and have traded wins over the NJPW Strong Women's Championship and the AEW TBS Championship.

At All In, they'll meet one-on-one yet again, this time for the AEW Women's World Championship. Nightingale won the title for the first time only a month ago at Redemption, while Moné secured her shot by capturing the women's Owen Hart Cup two years in a row.

All signs point to the third time being the charm for Moné (after failing in her previous opportunities at All In 2025 and Full Gear 2025) and her taking the title that has eluded her since her arrival in the promotion, but Nightingale retaining would be the more interesting outcome.

Moné falling short would force her "crash out" to continue, and effectively turn Nightingale from a perennial chaser to a certified champion. Moné ended Nightingale's TBS title run after only one month, but history shouldn't repeat itself here.

Nightingale will again have Moné's number and pull out the win against the odds.

Sheamus, Ilja Dragunov Debut in the Men's Casino Gauntlet

The New Day may not be the only ones making their first-ever AEW appearance at All In this weekend at Wembley Stadium.

Two more familiar faces who recently left WWE on their own terms and are presumably exploring new ventures are Sheamus and Ilja Dragunov. Both men's contracts recently expired after not being featured on WWE TV for many months.

Sheamus and Dragunov were known for their intense, hard-hitting style during their time in WWE and would be perfect fits for the AEW landscape. If they are free and clear of any contractual obligation to WWE, why not have them show up during the men's Casino Gauntlet match at All In?

One of them alone would make an immediate impact, but putting them both in the same bout would be the bigger shocker of them all, similar to how Adam Cole and Bryan Danielson debuted in AEW within minutes of each other at All Out in 2021. They wouldn't be overshadowed provided they're in there for long enough and are allowed to have strong showings.

Sheamus and Dragunov being "All Elite" is inevitable, and there would be no better time or place for them to make their presence felt and potentially punch their ticket to AEW World Championship contention out of the gate.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: The walls appeared to be closing in on Gianni Infantino. Not everyone wants him gone
articles.summary: Former soccer great Samuel Eto’o exclusively told CNN Sports that he thinks FIFA President Gianni Infantino has done nothing wrong and wants the controversial FFE proposal back on the table for discussion.
articles.body: In recent weeks, it might have felt inevitable that Gianni Infantino would be forced to resign as FIFA president. The walls were closing in on him, and the rising tide of criticism following his failed attempt to rush through his controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal seemed overwhelming. And yet, despite calls for him to step down still echoing around the sport, Infantino is still holding on to power with the FIFA presidential election fast approaching in March. And while some don’t want to wait that long to have the chance of toppling Infantino, the current FIFA boss does have some support swimming in the sea of objectors. One of those people is the president of the Cameroonian Football Federation (FECAFOOT) Samuel Eto’o, who recently told CNN Sports in an exclusive interview that Infantino hasn’t done anything wrong and actually called for the controversial plan that caused this tumultuous situation to be revisited. Eto’o was once one of the best players in the world, scoring countless goals and winning major trophies for the likes of Barcelona, Inter Milan, Chelsea and Real Madrid. He was elected FECAFOOT president in 2021 and has since set about growing the profile of both Cameroonian and African soccer as a whole. “I don’t think that President Gianni Infantino has done anything wrong,” Eto’o told CNN Sports when asked about the FIFA president’s conduct regarding the FFE plan. “I think the timing of all of that is because there’s an election coming out, when Gianni Infantino is standing. All of this has happened because there’s an election coming out, that’s all there is.” Eto’o’s voice will come as a welcome refuge for Infantino, who has been battered from pillar to post by a host of confederations. European body UEFA has threatened to boycott future tournaments, while the North & Central American and Caribbean governing body CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) demanded a change in leadership. The upcoming Under-20 Women’s World Cup in September could be the next flashpoint, with UEFA teams potentially not taking part. That would mean six of the qualified teams wouldn’t play, including the current host Poland. ‘Incredible’ FFE plan The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has been a rare backer of Infantino, although questions remain about which individual nations actually support its federation’s stance. Cameroon appears to be very much in line, and Infantino even name-checked Eto’o in a ‘thank-you post’ on Instagram last week. “President Gianni Infantino has changed football,” Eto’o added, urging fellow African nations to support the FIFA president. “He’s given opportunities to nations that didn’t have those opportunities to take part in the most beautiful tournament, the World Cup. He enabled smaller nations to get seats at these competitions. “He has helped our continent. He’s helped our federations to develop much more quickly, and we need to acknowledge that. We need to accept and recognize what he’s done, and we should support him for everything he’s done up to now.” Eto’o told CNN Sports the proposed plan would have helped distribute wealth in a fairer manner, allowing smaller nations to compete with the biggest in the world by having better facilities and resources. He said it would have helped teams like Cameroon to attract the best players in the world – such as Kylian Mbappé, who was born in France but who has Cameroonian heritage through his father. “There are federations in other continents that are in the same situation as us, that find themselves more or less at the same financial level as us to develop the football that we love so much. We want to see the (Lionel) Messis, we want to see the Mbappés, but I would like to see Mbappé play for Cameroon.” FIFA has already apologized for some of its actions and scrapped the FFE proposal. It also backed Infantino after a crisis meeting in Morocco last month. The narrative from FIFA now is that erroneous media reporting blew the proposed plans out of context, and that’s something echoed by Eto’o, who still thinks it was a good idea and hopes it can be debated if Infantino is reelected next year. “The bigger nations took up the media space. They gave their point of view, and President Gianni Infantino wanted to keep the family of football together, and he decided to withdraw the project,” he said. “I remain convinced that for us as Africans, this project was something that could have been incredible. It would have reset the balance of power in football to ensure that our talent doesn’t disappear and end up playing for other nations. “At the end of the day, those who have talked about the project and who’ve given their opinion haven’t properly read what it’s all about, and in some cases, they looked at it from their dominant position. He added: “I want to see all of my colleagues, all of the presidents, re-reading the project. After President Infantino is re-elected, we will have the strength to ask for this project to be put back on the table for discussion. “I remain convinced that, if there is a democratic vote, this project will be adopted because it’s good for the majority.” Support for Infantino Eto’o is not the only person banging the drum for Infantino in what’s become an increasingly fractured landscape. Support from CAF could be crucial, but there is also sympathy from other parts of the world. South America’s CONMEBOL has praised FIFA for scrapping its controversial plan but stopped short of calling for Infantino to resign. The Argentinian FA has also thrown its full weight behind the beleaguered leader. He also has support from Mexico (member of CONCACAF) and AFC members Qatar, Indonesia and the Philippines, showing how some national soccer associations are breaking away from the stance of their confederations. It’s a numbers game involving which of the 211 national associations are either for or against Infantino staying on. The election next year can’t come soon enough for some critics, although it’s not yet clear who would challenge Infantino – contenders need to come forward by the November 18 deadline. But there might be another way to push the leader out early. Should 20% of FIFA’s 211 member nations make a formal written request, an extraordinary congress would be called, as per FIFA’s statutes. A vote of no confidence in Infantino could then be launched, giving all members a chance to decide his fate – although CNN Sports could find no official guidelines about this potenital process. The walls were closing in on him, and the rising tide of criticism following his failed attempt to rush through his controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal seemed overwhelming. And yet, despite calls for him to step down still echoing around the sport, Infantino is still holding on to power with the FIFA presidential election fast approaching in March. And while some don’t want to wait that long to have the chance of toppling Infantino, the current FIFA boss does have some support swimming in the sea of objectors. One of those people is the president of the Cameroonian Football Federation (FECAFOOT) Samuel Eto’o, who recently told CNN Sports in an exclusive interview that Infantino hasn’t done anything wrong and actually called for the controversial plan that caused this tumultuous situation to be revisited. It also backed Infantino after a crisis meeting in Morocco last month. They gave their point of view, and President Gianni Infantino wanted to keep the family of football together, and he decided to withdraw the project,” he said. “I remain convinced that for us as Africans, this project was something that could have been incredible. He added: “I want to see all of my colleagues, all of the presidents, re-reading the project. The Argentinian FA has also thrown its full weight behind the beleaguered leader. It’s a numbers game involving which of the 211 national associations are either for or against Infantino staying on. articles.title: Jackson Hastings: St Helens captain given three-game ban for violent conduct that could end his season
articles.summary: St Helens keep their play-off hopes alive with victory over Castleford, despite Jackson Hastings' sending off for violent conduct; his Grade E offence for punching the Tigers' Tyler Dupree carries a three-game ban, meaning his season could be over if Saints fail to qualify
articles.body:
St Helens captain Jackson Hastings' season could be over after being handed a three-match ban for violent conduct following his sending off in their win over Castleford Tigers on Saturday.

Hastings was dismissed in the first half of the 36-12 victory after punching Castleford's Tyler Dupree, who was sin-binned for the same incident.

Commenting on Hastings' dismissal, Castleford director of rugby Chris Chester told Sky Sports: "Scott Murrell just jumped (in the way of Dupree). We all know the rules, you can't punch people in the face."

The win keeps Saints' play-off hopes alive, though they are currently on 28 points and seventh in the standings, one place outside of the play-off positions with three games to go.

It means that should they fail to leapfrog one of Hull KR (sixth, 30 points), Leigh Leopards (fifth, 32 points) or Wakefield Trinity (fourth, 32 points) down the stretch, Hastings will have played his last match of the season.

Current Super League leaders Leeds Rhinos, as well as Wigan Warriors - tied on 38 points but with an inferior point differential - and Warrington Wolves, two back in third, have already qualified for the play-offs.

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

articles.title: Four arrested over fatal shooting of South African boxer Zolani Tete
articles.summary: Tete, who won world WBF flyweight and WBO bantamweight titles, was killed outside his home in Eastern Cape last week.
articles.body:
South African police say they have arrested four people in connection with the murder of two-time boxing world champion Zolani Tete , who was shot last week.

The four suspects arrested over the weekend are aged between 22 and 28, police said in a statement on Monday. One has been formally charged with murder.

list 3 of 4 Boxer Chapman recovering after emergency surgery for brain bleed

list 4 of 4 UK police confirm Uganda boxers unaccounted for after Commonwealth Games

Tete, 38, was attacked on Friday evening as he returned to his home in Mdantsane in the Eastern Cape province.

A 27-year-old woman who was with him in the car survived but is in hospital, police said.

Tete won the IBF junior bantamweight world title in 2014 and the WBO bantamweight world title in 2017.

In 2017, he entered boxing history when he took just 11 seconds to flatten his opponent with his first punch to retain his WBO bantamweight crown.

It was the fastest knockout victory in a world championship bout.

In 2023, the United Kingdom Anti-Doping agency hit Tete with a four-year ban that ended on July 29, and he was preparing to return to professional boxing.

“South Africa has lost one of the finest fighters it has ever produced,” Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie said in a statement following the murder.

“He was training for a return to the ring. He believed he still had something to give this country. He was right, but he will not get the chance now. He, and all of us, have been robbed.”

articles.title: Samuel Eto’o urges support for embattled FIFA President Gianni Infantino
articles.summary: Former star striker, now head of Cameroon’s FA, backs Infantino despite mounting pressure on him to resign.
articles.body:
Former Cameroon star Samuel Eto’o has thrown his support behind beleaguered FIFA President Gianni Infantino , saying he “hasn’t done anything wrong” despite facing mounting pressure to step down over a controversial World Cup selloff plan.

Infantino has come under intense scrutiny since the collapse of a proposal to secure private investment in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup.

list 2 of 4 Salah scores two goals, has two disallowed in first start for Trabzonspor

list 3 of 4 Raphinha and Lopez score braces as Barcelona trounce Elche 5-0

list 4 of 4 Real Madrid’s Mourinho condemns bullying of Vinicius after La Liga win

UEFA, which oversees European football, has threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions, with several continental and national federations also withdrawing their support for Infantino.

However, Eto’o, president of the Cameroonian Football Federation, dismissed criticism of Infantino’s leadership, suggesting the backlash was driven largely by political manoeuvring ahead of FIFA’s presidential election next year.

“I don’t think that President Gianni Infantino has done anything wrong,” the former Barcelona, Inter Milan and Chelsea striker told CNN.

“I think the timing of all of that is because there’s an election coming out.”

Infantino’s plan, which would reportedly have distributed substantial funding to FIFA’s 211 member associations, faced strong opposition from several confederations and was ultimately abandoned.

The FIFA president remains under pressure, with the possibility of a no-confidence vote being triggered. UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), and the Confederation of North, Central American and Caribbean Association Football (CONCACAF) have all voiced concerns over FIFA’s direction in recent weeks.

But the Confederation of African Football (CAF) earlier this month “unanimously reconfirmed its support” for Infantino, and Eto’o’s backing is aligned with that position.

“President Gianni Infantino has changed football,” said Eto’o, urging fellow African countries to support the Swiss official.

“He’s given opportunities to nations that didn’t have those opportunities to take part in the most beautiful tournament, the World Cup. He enabled smaller nations to get seats at these competitions.

“He has helped our continent. He’s helped our federations to develop much more quickly, and we need to acknowledge that. We need to accept and recognise what he’s done, and we should support him for everything he’s done up to now.”

Meanwhile, a group of former international players, including World Cup winners and FIFA legends, called on Monday ⁠for immediate change at FIFA, saying its leadership under embattled Infantino had been blinded by power.

“We ‌share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” said former players including France’s 1998 men’s World Cup winners Emmanuel Petit, Bixente Lizarazu and Robert Pires as well as American former women’s world champion Briana Scurry and former England international Lucy Bronze.

“Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under FIFA’s current leadership. Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best ⁠for football,” the group said.

The group also includes ⁠former Peru forward Claudio Pizarro, former Argentina international Juan Sebastian Veron, former Togo captain Emmanuel Adebayor, and FIFA legends Didier Drogba and David James.

FIFA legends are former players recognised for their contributions to the sport who help promote football on behalf of the ⁠global body, playing in exhibition matches and supporting social and charity projects worldwide.

“We call on all stakeholders to step forward and help reshape the future ⁠of our sport. There are good people within FIFA who want ⁠to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structural change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run,” the group said.

Infantino is up for re-election next year, but world football’s regional powerhouses are discussing whether to move a ‌vote of no confidence in him ahead of the ballot, senior figures familiar with the discussions told the Reuters news agency last week.

“Those who step onto the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine ‌voice ‌to help reshape football’s future together. For the fans, for the players, and for the good of the game, we will be silent no more,” the players’ group said.

articles.title: England drop fast bowler Bryden Carse amid investigation into club incident
articles.summary: The 31-year-old Durham bowler will not play against Pakistan in the upcoming second Test match.
articles.body:
England fast bowler ‌Brydon Carse has been dropped from the squad for the second ⁠Test against ⁠Pakistan amid an investigation into an incident at a club in Derby, the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has said.

“Following a ⁠referral from the ECB, the Cricket Regulator has confirmed that they will investigate events on Saturday night in Derby,” the board said in a statement on Monday.

“Brydon ⁠Carse will no longer be available for selection for the second men’s test while this investigation is ongoing and the full facts are obtained.”

Carse, who did not play in the opening test victory at Headingley, will be replaced by Sonny ‌Baker.

Videos circulated on social media appearing to show the 31-year-old Durham bowler in handcuffs being spoken to by police officers outside a venue. According to reports, Carse was not arrested and no charges were brought.

It has been a busy summer for England’s Cricket Regulator, the body set up to investigate matters where there is an allegation of a breach of ⁠the ECB’s code of conduct.

In June, it concluded an ⁠investigation into former test captain Ben Stokes and fast bowler Gus Atkinson after a nightclub incident following the first test against New Zealand.

Both were left out of the second test before ⁠the regulator ruled that there was insufficient evidence to establish that any regulatory breach occurred.

The latest investigation comes five ⁠days after England’s returning test captain Joe Root ⁠spoke of the players being “really good role models and human beings” following a series of incidents and accusations of a drinking culture.

Controversy has followed England recently, with off-field issues ‌during last winter’s tours – including Harry Brook being fined 30,000 pounds ($41,000) following an altercation in Wellington, New Zealand – as well as reports of drinking during a mid-Ashes series trip ‌to ‌Noosa.

Stokes retired from international cricket after returning for the third test against New Zealand and Brendon McCullum was sacked as test coach.

articles.title: Former snooker world champion Graeme Dott convicted of child sex abuse
articles.summary: The 49-year-old was found to have subjected a girl and a boy to multiple incidents of abuse.
articles.body:
Former snooker world champion Graeme Dott has been convicted of sexually abusing two children several decades ago in a trial in ⁠a Scottish court.

Dott was charged with two counts of “lewd, indecent and libidinous behaviour” ⁠against a girl from 1993 to 1996 and a boy from 2006 to 2010.

The indictment alleged that the 49-year-old had sexually assaulted the girl, ‌exposed himself to her and induced her to touch him. Dott was also accused of making sexual remarks to the boy and touching his genitals.

He denied the charges but was found guilty on Monday after a trial ⁠at the High Court ⁠in Glasgow. He will be sentenced next month.

“Dott is a dangerous individual, and I hope this conviction provides some ⁠measure of comfort to those impacted by his crimes,” Detective Inspector ⁠Gary Smillie from Police ⁠Scotland told reporters.

Dott won the world snooker championship in 2006, beating Peter Ebdon 18-14 in the final, and ‌finished as runner-up in 2004 and 2010.

He was suspended by the World Professional Billiards and ‌Snooker ‌Association after the charges were announced last year.

articles.title: San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York arrested for ‘engaging in prostitution’ and later charged with disorderly conduct
articles.summary: The principal owner of the NFL’s San Francisco 49ers was arrested on Sunday and accused of “engaging in prostitution” in Ohio, according to court documents obtained by CNN.
articles.body: The principal owner of the NFL’s San Francisco 49ers was arrested on Sunday and accused of “engaging in prostitution” in Ohio, according to court documents obtained by CNN. Jed York, who’s been with the team for nearly 20 years, became the chief executive officer in 2010. According to the court documents, York pleaded no contest to the charges of disorderly conduct and possession of criminal tools after being detained in East Palestine. The documents state York paid $1,150 in fines associated with the charges and sentenced to a night in jail. CNN has reached out to the 49ers and York’s legal team for comment. NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy said in a statement, “We are aware of the matter which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy.” Columbiana County records show York had $160 seized and not returned to the team owner, but instead “forfeited” to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the plea agreement. The records also list that York completed an online course, though the specific nature of the course is not stated. The 46-year-old is the oldest son of Denise and John York, the co-chairmen of the 49ers. This story has been updated with additional reporting.

NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy said in a statement, “We are aware of the matter which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy.” Columbiana County records show York had $160 seized and not returned to the team owner, but instead “forfeited” to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the plea agreement. The records also list that York completed an online course, though the specific nature of the course is not stated. The 46-year-old is the oldest son of Denise and John York, the co-chairmen of the 49ers. This story has been updated with additional reporting.

articles.title: Panthers Expect RB Chuba Hubbard To Be Ready For Week 1
articles.summary: Panthers starting running back Chuba Hubbard injured his hamstring earlier in training camp.
articles.body: The Panthers' running back room is full of questions entering the 2026 season, but one of those has seemingly been answered. Coach Dave Canales said on Monday that the expectation is that injured back Chuba Hubbard will be ready for Week 1, per the Associated Press. Hubbard is expected to be the starting running back with Jonathon Brooks the second option, but a strained hamstring suffered during training camp has kept Hubbard from appearing in a single preseason game to this point. Due to that – and Hubbard not yet focusing on cutting due to the Panthers' caution, per Canales' own admission – the duo will work in a running back by committee approach to begin the year, per The Athletic.  A calf injury limited Hubbard in 2025, which cost him starts in favor of Rico Dowdle: Hubbard appeared in 15 games but started just the first six, and went from averaging 13.2 attempts and 47 yards per game to 6.1 rushes and 25.4 yards per over his last nine appearances. NFL Related StoriesCleveland Browns Name Deshaun Watson The Starting QBNFL Catchup: Jeanty Injured, Kittle Activated, Browns QB Drama & More49ers, Saints Reportedly Swap Depth Pieces In A Trade Ahead Of Regular Season Dowdle, though, signed with the Pittsburgh Steelers this offseason, opening space back up for Hubbard, as well as the returning Brooks. A second-round pick in 2024, Brooks appeared in just three games as a rookie before the 21-year-old suffered a second torn ACL and missed the rest of that season and the subsequent one recovering. Now healthy, he is listed as the second back on the Panthers' depth chart, ahead of Trevor Etienne, AJ Dillon and Anthony Tyrus III, though, Brooks has just eight carries so far this preseason. In 2024, his last healthy season, Hubbard had 250 rushing attempts for 1,195 yards and 10 touchdowns in 15 games, all starts. A fourth-round pick in the 2021 NFL Draft, he has spent his entire career with the Panthers,

articles.title: Ex-Liverpool star Fabinho reunited with Mohamed Salah at Trabzonspor
articles.summary: Fabinho joined Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ittihad in 2023, where he won the league after his five-year stint at Liverpool.
articles.body:
Brazil ⁠midfielder Fabinho has ⁠signed a two-year deal with Trabzonspor, the Turkish Super Lig football side has announced, and will link up with ⁠former Liverpool teammate Mohamed Salah .

The 32-year-old midfielder will receive a 2.6-million-euro ($3.03m) guaranteed fee and a 1.4-million-euro ($1.63m) signing ⁠fee per season, according to a Turkish stock exchange filing made by the team on Monday.

“An agreement has been reached for a two-year contract with … Fabinho, who is currently in free status,” Trabzonspor posted on ‌X.

Fabinho joined Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ittihad in 2023 and helped the team win the domestic league after his five-year stint at Liverpool.

“A really special feeling to be playing with Salah again … I had the opportunity to play with him for five years in Liverpool. He is a person whom I respect a lot both for ⁠what he has done and what he ⁠will do,” Fabinho said after arriving at Trabzon airport earlier on Monday.

Looking to reignite his chemistry with 34-year-old Salah, Fabinho said: “I will always try to do the ⁠best I can with whatever ability I have.

“Along with the experience and leadership that come from ⁠playing for so many years, I will ⁠always try to help my teammates.”

Fabinho made 219 appearances for Liverpool, helping it win the Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup, League Cup, Club World Cup and UEFA Super Cup ‌titles.

Egypt forward Salah joined Trabzonspor as a free agent earlier this month.

Trabzonspor finished third in the Turkish top flight last season, and take on Hungary’s Ferencvaros on Thursday in the second leg of their Europa League playoff tie, trailing 1-0.

articles.title: 'An unfortunate racket': As India nears its 100th chess Grandmaster, is an expensive coach all you need?
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: In 1978, the chess world was a reflection of a fiercely guarded aristocracy, it can be said. The title of Grandmaster (GM) was not merely a.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In 1978, the chess world was a reflection of a fiercely guarded aristocracy, it can be said. The title of Grandmaster (GM) was not merely a designation. Rather, it was an exclusive fraternity reserved for the absolute statistical anomalies of the human race.To understand what has happened to the modern chess ecosystem, one must first understand what a Grandmaster used to be. To many historians, the very definition of chess mastery has been fundamentally altered."A Grandmaster result has been a performance equivalent to a 2600 rating. In 1978, there were only six players above 2600. And in 1981, I think there were about twelve or thirteen. So a 2600 performance essentially boiled down to doing as well as the top six or seven or ten players in the world," India's veteran Grandmaster Pravin Thipsay told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction.The rating inflation over the ensuing decades has been astronomical. Thipsay believes a 2600 rating in the early 1980s was the equivalent of a 2750 rating today, a tier reserved exclusively for the absolute best in the business today.Yet, the threshold to earn the GM title remains anchored to the 2600 performance. "Which means the International Master (IM) norm in the 1980s or in the '70s was more difficult than today's Grandmaster title," Thipsay added with a smile.Many feel it has not been an organic evolution of the sport but a deliberate, commercial policy choice.Between 1914 and 1997, the world produced fewer than 300 Grandmasters. But in 1998, under the leadership of then-FIDE President Kirsan Ilyumzhinov, the governing body prioritised global expansion. The criteria for titles were relaxed, and the rating floor, once a jaw-dropping mark of 2200, was eventually plummeted to 1000 (before settling at 1400 more recently in 2024).By 2004, the world had 1,000 Grandmasters. Today, there are over 2,500."FIDE started collecting fees for rated players," Thipsay noted, outlining the financial incentive behind the dilution. "It became an important way of getting money for FIDE during Kirsan's time. He specifically made it clear in the Congress in 1998 and 2000 that we want to lower down the title, we want to lower down the rating. He said, 'We want to make everything easy for you so that you can find sponsors more easily.'"The Indian explosionAgainst this backdrop of global title inflation, India stands on the precipice of a historic milestone.In a matter of weeks, if not days, the nation will crown its 100th Grandmaster. It is a sumptuous achievement for a country that waited until 1988 for Viswanathan Anand to become its first.Today, India is an undeniable superpower as it keeps on churning out prodigies who casually dismantle the worldâs elite.But beneath the glittering surface of this golden generation lies a complex, often unspoken reality.As FIDE titles and ratings became vastly more accessible, the grassroots culture of the sport underwent a radical, heavily commercialised shift. The gritty, egalitarian days of the game have gradually evaporated, replaced by an ecosystem catered strictly to the affluent."There were tournaments where everybody played, everybody stayed in a dormitory, and 80%, 90% of the money collected would go for the prize money," Thipsay recalled. "Organisers like YMCA provided halls and dormitory accommodation free, and people didn't really bother. I remember 40, 50 people staying together for my National Juniors, and nobody really grumbled about it."Today, things are different. One-day rapid tournaments routinely charge entry fees of Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000. Organisers rake in lakhs, while prize funds remain disproportionately small."By keeping such high entry fee, you have actually ended up making it a sport for rich people," Thipsay argued. "A common man, a child of a clerk or a laborer is not able to play even a one-day tournament irrespective of the prize. The entire chess-playing crowd has become the elite class who can afford such luxurious tournaments."The "complacency in mediocrity"Because FIDE ratings are now easily obtained, a dangerous phenomenon has taken root in Indian society. It is what Thipsay terms "complacency in mediocrity".Getting a rating today is, in his words, "probably one of the easiest things", achievable by a child after just a year of play. Yet, parents treat it as a monumental triumph.Drunk on early, low-level success, families make drastic life decisions. "Parents think, and the players think that they are good players; they are going to become Grandmasters very soon," Thipsay said."Grandmaster is everybody's ambition, whereas I think the title has not been lowered down to that level that everybody can become Grandmaster. Needless to say, there are many players who give up their studies and try their best in playing, and they end up remaining at the rating level of 1500 to 1700. Most of the players who played chess for thousands of hours, not going to school, remain between 1500 to 1800 level. And now they already have a bad academic record."With limited professional options outside the sport, these stalled players pivot to the only available avenue, which is coaching.This massive supply of trainers has birthed a sprawling, unregulated industry. Parents are liquidating assets and funnelling lakhs of rupees into private coaching, convinced it is the only path to the GM title."A need for coaching does not exist, but it is created," Thipsay, a renowned coach himself, remarked. "The way the coaching takes place is basically spoon-feeding rather than teaching chess."The doctrines of the legends like Dr Emanuel Lasker and Garry Kasparov, who preached that chess cannot merely be taught, tell us that the sole duty of a coach is to cultivate independent thinking."If you see, out of one lakh players, only three or four are able to think independently," Thipsay told this website. "We often have to de-train students for two to three years. An untrained child is much easier to teach than a trained child who is often on a wrong track."Further stressing the notion of independent thinking, he added, "Itâs very easy to become a Grandmaster if there is group discussion, if players come together, meet and discuss among themselves. All they need is the process of independent thinking. We need a coach who coaches, say, for 10 hours and teaches them to think independently."You will not have everybody becoming a Grandmaster. But many of the International Masters in the country would probably have become Grandmasters even without coaching, if they had decided to sit down together and analyse. Many of them may already be doing that as well."Itâs very easy to become a Grandmaster if there is group discussion, if players come together, meet and discuss among themselves.Nevertheless, the ongoing chess boom has perpetuated the general idea that an aspiring player must spend a heavy amount on elite coaching to reach the pinnacle."It's only a myth, and it's created to promote the coaches," Thipsay said, pointing out that players like R Praggnanandhaa, D Gukesh, and Aravindh Chithambaram became top-level Grandmasters without spending exorbitant sums on coaching early on.Furthermore, the financial return on investment is bleak.The veteran GM revealed, "The average income of an Indian Grandmaster through winnings in chess tournaments is less than one and a half lakhs per year. It's something I would call an unfortunate racket rather than expensive coaching."The pure talent argumentIs Thipsay right? Is the modern coaching industrial complex entirely a racket?Grandmaster Aravindh Chithambaram, a multiple-time National Champion known for his immense natural talent and humble beginnings, pushes back slightly on the idea that exorbitant wealth is a prerequisite, but he acknowledges the steep climb."Not necessarily I feel like one can become a Grandmaster only if he spends 20 lakhs or 30 lakhs," Aravindh told TimesofIndia.com."I think if a person is really skillful, he can achieve no matter what. But of course, the initial stages would be very hard. Because if you're not a Grandmaster or even an International Master, of course you will have to spend a lot of money. But once you make the first step, I think the rest of them would be easier comparatively. The first step would be very hard, I would say. But once you understand that you are skillful, you have the talent playing, then things are much easier."For players of Aravindh's calibre, raw skill eventually attracts sponsors, mitigating the financial burden.But for those who don't possess generation-defining talent, the necessity of a coach is less about "spoon-feeding" and more about an invaluable, finite resource like time.The pragmatic truth of the "Engine Era"Delhi's Aaryan Varshney, who recently became Indiaâs 92nd Grandmaster, offers a compelling counterweight to Thipsayâs purist philosophy.Varshneyâs journey is highly unusual. He reached the GM title at 21 without a formal academy, expensive foreign trainers, or a titled coach.Instead, he was guided entirely by his father, Gaurav, a single parent who left his job to study the game alongside his son. Yet, despite his DIY success story, Varshney is adamant that going it completely alone in the modern era is a mistake."If someone really wants to become GM, then they have to have someone who can sit with them and analyse games, sometimes all night, like my father did," Varshney told this website."A coach wouldn't necessarily do as much as my father did. But you need someone, at the very least. You can't do everything completely on your own. I didn't do anything. I'm telling you from my own experience. My father did the whole thing for me. So, doing everything yourself makes the journey difficult. You need a coach."If you're doing something yourself, something that might take us five hours, a coach can get you to do it in one hour.To Varshney, the value of a coach is not in inflating a player's ego, but in condensing the gruelling hours of modern computer engine analysis."It's not necessary for your coach to be an IM or a GM. The important thing is that the coach should be good, someone who can actually teach the child," Varshney pointed out. "If you're doing something yourself, something that might take us five hours, a coach can get you to do it in one hour. Would you rather spend five hours or one hour? Obviously, everyone would prefer one hour."Varshney's reality check underlines the modern burden placed on young players."Even analysing games yourself becomes difficult, because when you look at the engine, you can get stuck trying to understand why a particular move is good," Varshney explained. "Someone who already has that knowledge can explain it to you easily. Whatever I was struggling to understand, my father would explain it to me in two minutes. Otherwise, I would just sit there trying to figure it out."As India approaches its 100th Grandmaster, the ecosystem supporting these players remains a paradox.Thipsay is undeniably right. The title is statistically easier to obtain than it was in 1978, and the fear-mongering that demands parents spend lakhs on coaching is, in many cases, a predatory racket preying on affluent families.Yet, Varshneyâs lived experience proves that in the modern computer era, navigating the labyrinth of chess theory without a guide is a punishing task.Also Read: Gave up IIT, left home, slept on roads: How Rajasthan's first AGM put Udaipur on global chess mapA player does not need an exorbitant, six-figure coaching setup to become a Grandmaster. But they do need a translator for the digital age.India will soon celebrate its 100th Grandmaster. But behind the celebratory headlines, the true challenge will remain as to how the ecosystem ensures the sport remains a battle of minds, rather than a battle of bank accounts.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mike McCarthy Admits Steelers, CB Joey Porter Jr. Remain At 'Impasse' Over New Deal
articles.summary: Mike McCarthy wants to work with Joey Porter Jr., but the Pittsburgh Steelers and the cornerback are at an impasse over a new deal.
articles.body: Mike McCarthy wants the chance to work with Joey Porter Jr. When McCarthy gets that chance is anyone's guess, the Pittsburgh Steelers coach included. McCarthy said Monday that the club and the fourth-year cornerback are at an impasse as the two sides try to work out a new deal. The Steelers placed Porter on the physically unable to perform list when training camp opened with what the team described as a back issue that flared up during a mobility test. It seems Porter's back problems are just part of the reason he has yet to take the practice field with the season opener against Atlanta less than three weeks away. "I learned this in my early years as a head coach, you have to separate the business from the football," McCarthy said. "Sometimes it’s easier than others." Porter is in the final season of the four-year deal he signed after the Steelers selected him with the first pick of the second round in 2023. While Pittsburgh has locked up other members of that draft class — including outside linebacker Nick Herbig and tight end Darnell Washington — Porter's status seems a little more uncertain. The 26-year-old is coming off his best season as a pro, and he said during minicamp in June that he long felt he's one of the top players at his position and that he believes he will be paid that way. The top of the cornerback market has been particularly hot of late, with Seattle’s Devon Witherspoon agreeing to a massive new deal and New England’s Christian Gonzalez getting offered one in recent weeks. Though Porter, who has three interceptions across three seasons, might not be in that neighborhood yet, he also might not be far off. articles.title: Former NBA players not eligible for WNBA, sources say
articles.summary: Former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White are not eligible to play in the WNBA, sources around the league confirm.
articles.body: Former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White are not eligible to play in the WNBA, sources around the league told CNN on Monday. ESPN was first to report on the news. Both men announced last month that they now identify as women and said they planned to enter the 2027 WNBA draft amid a national conversation surrounding gender eligibility policies and transgender inclusion in women’s sports. However, no transgender women have played in the WNBA. The sources firmly rejected the draft declarations, characterizing them as publicity stunts designed to mock the league, sow division, and draw attention to the topic by demeaning others. There are no legitimate or immediate eligibility matters requiring action by the WNBA at this time, the sources said. The league has said it plans to approach the broader topic “thoughtfully” alongside its primary stakeholders, including players, teams and the union, and would not allow “outside pressure or manufactured controversy to dictate” its internal processes or force a response to efforts intended to demean others. On Sunday, Freedom was ejected after a high-profile courtside incident at Wintrust Arena in Chicago. During the third quarter of the Indiana Fever and Chicago Sky game, Freedom, who was seated along the baseline wearing a shirt bearing the definition of a woman, got into a heated verbal exchange with Sky guard Natasha Cloud. “It’s always women hating on other women,” Freedom posted on X after the game. No formal announcement or disciplinary ruling regarding a potential game ban for Freedom has been made.

articles.title: WWE Raw Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights From Aug. 24
articles.summary: WWE rolled into the Canadian Tire Centre in Ottawa for the August 24 episode of Raw, headlined by a contract signing featuring Oba Femi and Bron Breakker.
articles.body:
WWE rolled into the Canadian Tire Centre in Ottawa for the August 24 episode of Raw, headlined by a contract signing featuring Oba Femi and Bron Breakker.

What went down when they shared the same ring in a highly combustible situation?

Find out in this recap of Monday's show, including grades and analysis for the night's No. 1 contender's tournament match-ups.

Announced in advance of Monday's show were:

No. 1 Contender's Tournament Match: Rey Fenix vs. Dragon Lee

No. 1 Contender's Tournament Match: Penta vs. La Parka

Oba Femi and Bron Breakker contract signing

Last Time In Action: LA Knight, Solo Sikoa, and Royce Keys defeated The Bloodline (SummerSlam, August 1)

LA Knight and Solo Sikoa sent a warning shot to The Bloodline after dropping Roman Reigns and The Usos last week, kicking off the show with an in-ring promo that perfectly blended humor and serious, story-advancing work.

Interrupted by Jimmy and Jey Uso, though, the united duo accepted a challenge for a main event match later in the show and got the last word, to the delight of the fans.

A solid segment that showcased Sikoa's enormous personality, this was a great follow-up to last week's show-closing segment, on a night when the OTC is not scheduled to appear.

Sikoa was genuinely funny here. His impersonation of Knight was outstanding and his Matrix reaction to Jey's "warning shot" was right out of Scary Movie . He's going to become a huge babyface star for WWE.

Knight is doing some of his best work right now. He seems motivated by his spot, a spot that should have been his far sooner than it is.

Last Time in Action: Stephanie Vaquer lost to Liv Morgan (WrestleMania, April 18); Roxanne Perez and Raquel Rodriguez lost to Iyo Sky and Sol Ruca (Raw, August 10)

Stephanie Vaquer scored her first victory in her first match in four months, defeating The Judgment Day's Roxanne Perez in singles competition on Monday.

The Prodigy put up a tough fight, working over La Primera, who showed some signs of ring rust but shook it off for the most part down the stretch.

Overcoming interference from Women's World Champion Liv Morgan and Women's Intercontinental Champion Raquel Rodriguez, Vaquer downed Perez, thanks to the arrival of Becky Lynch, and earned the win to continue building momentum toward a championship opportunity.

After the match, Lynch and Vaquer exchanged words, keeping the tension between them alive in what is becoming one of the best programs on the Raw brand.

Perez is almost wasted in this role. The issues between her and Morgan are nearly non-existent at this point. She has largely become the tackling dummy for the Judgment Day, working matches and losing them as part of everyone else's story. One of the best wrestlers in the company, hopefully that trend changes sooner rather than later.

Vaquer looked good in her first match in four months. She looked a tad slower, but that ring rust will be erased the more ring time she gets in the coming weeks and months.

Last Time in Action: Dragon Lee defeated El Hijo del Dr. Wagner Jr. (Raw, August 17); Rey Fenix defeated El Fiscal (Raw, August 17)

Two of the best luchadors in professional wrestling squared off in the semifinals of the No. 1 Contender's Tournament, a chance to challenge Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship on September 14 in Mexico City, on the line, as AAA Cruiserweight Champion Rey Fenix battled Dragon Lee.

Chants of "this is awesome" rained from the stands as Lee launched himself through the ropes with a tope suicida and wiped Fenix out on the announce table. Back in the ring, he delivered a big DDT for two.

Fenix delivered a rolling cutter to a charging Lee, then added the Mexican Muscle Buster for the pinfall victory to cash his ticket to the finals of the tournament.

This was an excellent match that highlighted two woefully underutilized talents. Fans in Montreal were red hot for everything they did, and the result was an enhanced experience that proved that sometimes the best thing WWE can do to win over the audience is to let two extraordinary in-ring talents deliver between the ropes.

How many times does Lee have to show up and show out before enjoying a sustained push?

Are we really going to get a Fenix vs. Penta match before we ever see them team up as the Lucha Bros? It certainly looks that way.

Oba Femi and Bron Breakker Sign on the Dotted Line

Last Time In Action: Oba Femi defeated Brock Lesnar (SummerSlam, August 1); Bron Breakker defeated Joe Hendry (Raw, August 3)

Ahead of their showdown on September 6 at Sunday Night's Main Event, Oba Femi and World Tag Team Champion Bron Breakker met in the squared circle to sign the contract for their encounter.

Femi told Breakker that if he debuted in 2002 or 2014, he would have been the future of the industry. Unfortunately, he came around in 2026 and has the unenviable task of encountering The Ruler.

Breakker claimed that he would prove that he is the one guy Femi cannot beat.

The heel continued the narrative that Paul Heyman may be more closely aligned to Femi, angrily demanding the advocate sign for The Ruler.

He used that distraction as an opportunity to deliver a cheap shot before Austin Theory arrived on the scene. A two-on-one beatdown ensued before Femi powered out, sent Breakker to the floor, and drove his tag team partner through the table.

This was a strong segment, with Femi shining on the mic. To borrow a phrase used more frequently on WWE TV, he dog-walked Breakker, outshining him on the mic. He looked confident and comfortable while his opponent on SNME stumbled once or twice while cutting a more generic promo.

Femi referenced Roman Reigns, saying that Breakker would have been the future guy had he debuted in 2014 and gone up against "whoever the 'big dog' was at that time." Oh yeah...that match is going to slap when it finally happens.

Just in case you did not know what Theory's role was in the Vision, him going through the table as an afterthought was should have confirmed it for you.

Last Time in Action: Je'Von Evans defeated JD McDonagh (Raw, August 17); Big Cass lost to Daniel Bryan (Money in the Bank, June 17, 2018)

Big Cass wrestled his first match in eight years, battling Je'Von Evans and potentially biting off more than he could chew.

His size and strength advantage was negated at times by The Young OG's speed and creativity, and he was forced to fight from underneath late in the match-up.

The NXT export caught Evans, knocked him from the top rope to the ring apron, and rocked him with a big boot to the face to score the win, his lip busted and bloodied as evidence of the grueling competition he had just endured.

Booking Cass to go 50-50 with Evans was certainly a choice considering he just made his return, but The Young OG is not someone you want getting run over at this point in his career, either.

Considering the corner WWE Creative booked itself into, this was a fine match that highlighted both men and gave Cass a strong victory.

After the match, Judgment Day's Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh attacked, hinting at the next program for Evans.

Cass looked great for a guy wrestling his first match in a WWE ring in eight years. There are a lot of fans unfamiliar with his work as W. Morrissey and Big Bill, but he is a much better, more polished wrestler than he was nearly a decade ago.

Evans vs. Judgment Day is a logical next step. The question is who will step up and join the babyface against the hated heels.

No. 1 Contender's Match: Penta vs. La Parka

Last Time in Action: Penta defeated Bronco Nima (AAA, August 15); La Parka lost to EK Prosper in a Fatal 4-Way Match (NXT, August 18)

With a date against Rey Fenix in the finals of the No. 1 Contender's Tournament at stake, former Intercontinental Champion Penta battled La Parka in the night's penultimate match-up.

La Parka unloaded his arsenal on Penta, delivering an avalanche Spanish Fly and trying for the Bone Breaker. The latter countered, delivered the Sacrifice, and delivered a springboard Mexican Destroyer to score the win and set up a match with his brother on next week's show.

A fine match that paled in comparison to its predecessor earlier in the show, it was hampered by a lack of drama. Penta has been the obvious tournament winner since the bracket was announced. Losing to La Parka, in the latter's first Monday Night Raw appearance, was never a consideration.

The Lucha Bros explode next week in a match that should be a legitimate contender for WWE TV Match of the Year, if it is given enough time and the siblings are allowed to go all out.

La Parka is such an iconic character that this is one instance where a video package introducing him to the masses would have made for a hotter and more invested crowd.

Last Time in Action: LA Knight, Solo Sikoa, and Royce Keys defeated The Bloodline (SummerSlam, August 1); Jey Uso defeated Sikoa (Raw, August 10)

Royce Keys returned Monday night on Raw and brought OTM's Lucien Price and Bronco Nima with him.

Driven to desperate measures by the attack by The Bloodline that left him bleeding and out of action, Keys led the former NXT tag team in a brutal beatdown of The Usos, LA Knight, and Solo Sikoa, putting an exclamation point on the flagship show.

The shocking return came at the end of a high-profile tag team main event that saw Jimmy and Jey isolate Sikoa before a hot tag to Knight sparked the babyface comeback. Before a winner could be determined, the run-in occurred, resulting in a no contest.

It was a hot close to the show, the crowd in Montreal reacted accordingly, and there is suddenly intrigue at the top of the Raw brand, something there was not an abundance of heading into this week's broadcast.

Suddenly, Keys is a top-tier star, there is an interesting new team around, and The Bloodline's dominance does not look like a given.

Keys showed more personality in this beatdown than he did the entirety of his first few months with the company. That bodes well and shows that there is more to him than being a big, tough heavyweight.

On a night that featured some solid storyline advancement, it was Fenix and Lee's barnburner of a match that stood out and earned the competitors MVP honors.

They took what could have been a forgettable semifinal tournament match and turned it into one of the better TV efforts in a while.

Both are criminally overlooked and underutilized, so hopefully, this is an opportunity to give them something meaningful to do moving forward.

There was a lot to like about this show, with some better-than-expected story stuff, some quality in-ring action, and a big angle at the end of the show to send fans home satisfied.

Not everything hit, but the positive far outweighed the negative, and given the lethargic card for the night, that is a big win in and of itself.

articles.body: Taylor Fritz and Olivia Jade Giannulli have found themselves at the center of fresh romance rumors after being spotted together in New York City, just days before the 2026 US Open. The American tennis star and the social media influencer have been linked since May, but neither has publicly confirmed that they are a couple. Their latest sighting, however, has added another layer to a relationship that both sides have so far kept fairly quiet.Sources told TMZ that Fritz and Olivia are spending time together on a romantic level, although they are not rushing to put a label on things. The pair was reportedly seen together in New York over the weekend, with Fritz picking Olivia up before they headed to his hotel. For now, the reports suggest two people getting to know each other and seeing where the connection goes.Are Taylor Fritz and Olivia Jade dating?The answer is still unconfirmed, but the signs have become harder to ignore. Fritz and Olivia first sparked dating rumors in May after they were reportedly spotted together at The Bird Streets Club in West Hollywood. An anonymous submission to Deuxmoi claimed the pair was âlooking cozyâ during the outing.At the time, the situation appeared much less serious. A source told TMZ that the meeting was friendly and said Taylor âisnât even looking to get into another relationship.â That picture appears to have changed, at least somewhat, in the months since.The latest reports indicate that Fritz and Olivia have been âhanging out on a romantic level.â Sources also told TMZ they are âtaking things slow and enjoying their time together.â Neither has publicly defined the relationship, so it would be premature to call them an official couple.Their recent New York appearance has nevertheless fueled the speculation. Fritz is in the city for the US Open, while Olivia has also been spending time there. That has given the two plenty of opportunities to see each other away from the spotlight.Who is Taylor Fritzâs rumored girlfriend Olivia Jade?Olivia Jade is a social media influencer and the daughter of actress Lori Loughlin. She has built a large following online, with more than 1.2 million followers on Instagram, and has also attracted plenty of attention through her past relationships.Before being linked with Fritz, Olivia was involved in an on-and-off relationship with actor Jacob Elordi. The pair first sparked romance rumors in 2021 and continued to be linked at different points before their relationship eventually ended.Reports later connected Elordi with Kendall Jenner, while Olivia was also the subject of other dating speculation. She was reportedly seen with Braxton Berrios at a music festival and was previously linked to actor Glen Powell. Neither of those rumors developed into a confirmed long-term relationship.That history makes the Fritz connection another chapter in a dating life that has often played out under public scrutiny.Taylor Fritzâs relationship historyFritz is no stranger to having his personal life closely followed by tennis fans. Before Olivia, he dated influencer Morgan Riddle for nearly six years.Fritz and Riddle began dating in June 2020, and their relationship became closely tied to the growing lifestyle around professional tennis. articles.title: Former Celtics, Jazz Player RJ Luis Jr. Cleared By Judge To Play For LSU
articles.summary: Former St. John's standout RJ Luis Jr. has been cleared by a court to start practicing with LSU and potentially play for the Tigers this season.
articles.body: RJ Luis Jr., a former St. John's standout who recently signed with LSU after spending time with two NBA clubs, was cleared by a court Monday evening to start practicing and potentially play for the Tigers this season. Luis, who briefly was under contract with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics but never played in an NBA game, hugged LSU coach Will Wade after the ruling by East Baton Rouge Parish District Court judge Ronald R. Johnson. After a five-hour hearing, Johnson granted the player's request for a preliminary injunction against the NCAA, which had argued Luis was unlikely to win reinstatement after leaving college to turn pro in 2025. "This is precedent. It's monumental," said Baton Rouge-based attorney Tony Clayton, who represented Luis along with Elliot Abrams of Raleigh, North Carolina. "This allows him to go practice, go play and we'll let the legal process work itself out." The timeline for that process was not immediately clear. "I don't know, but there's a lot of discovery that Elliot and I have to obtain," Clayton said. "We've got a lot of questions." Luis' attorneys noted that the NCAA had granted exceptions allowing numerous players from overseas professional leagues to join college basketball programs, and argued that American players must be afforded the same opportunity. They stressed that Luis not only had never played in an NBA game, but also had not played for the Celtics' G League affiliate because of an injury, and had far less of a professional basketball resume than numerous college players who'd been recruited from abroad. NCAA attorney Taylor Askew argued that Luis' situation was not comparable to those who played for the developmental squads of pro organizations overseas because Luis chose to leave college for the NBA. Askew noted that the only player in a similar situation to Luis was Alabama's Charles Bediako, who won a temporary retraining order allowing him to play five games for Alabama last season before an Alabama judge ultimately sided with NCAA assertions that he was ineligible. "I understand Mr. Luis is disappointed that he was not drafted and did not play in the NBA as much as he would have liked," Askew said. "Actions have consequences. Decisions have outcomes and they're not always the right ones or the ones that you want." As he made his ruling, Johnson said, "In the court's mind, (Luis) did not actually play professional basketball," and that whether Luis was properly advised of his options at the time he left college "lingers heavily before this court." Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Angel Reese breaks WNBA record with 26 rebounds in Dream’s win over Sparks
articles.summary: Reese broke Chamique Holdsclaw’s record of 24 rebounds and added 11 points for her 27th double-double of the season.
articles.body:
Angel Reese broke the WNBA single-game rebounding record with 26, while also breaking the league’s season record for rebounds, as the Atlanta Dream beat the Los Angeles Sparks.

Reese surpassed Chamique Holdsclaw’s record of 24 rebounds, set on May 23, 2003 for the Washington Mystics, in the Dream’s 78-71 win on Monday .

The Dream star has 458 rebounds this season, seven more than A’ja Wilson’s mark set in 2024.

“Last time I was here, I didn’t miss any shots. Tonight I couldn’t hit (anything), so I knew I was going to be able to get them on the rebounding side,” Reese told the postgame show. “I just want to be there for my team. Offensively, defensively, whatever it takes to win.”

Reese finished with 11 points. She secured her WNBA-leading 27th double-double of the season on a basket with 13.9 seconds left in the game.

“That’s a talent,” Dream guard Allisha Gray said. “I’m just in awe watching her rebound.”

A three-time WNBA All-Star, Reese set a WNBA rookie record with 13.1 rebounds per game and the all-time league record with 15 straight double-doubles with Chicago in 2024. She led the league in rebounding her first two seasons and is leading again this season at 12.0 per game.

The Dream have beaten the Sparks nine straight times.

Gray led Atlanta (25-13) with 20 points. Rhyne Howard added 18 points to eclipse 3,000 for her career. Gray set an Atlanta record for field goals in a season with 247.

Nneka Ogwumike had 27 points and 16 rebounds for Los Angeles (13-25). Dearica Hamby and Cameron Brink each scored 15 points.

articles.title: Fulham vs Chelsea: Alonso starts new era with thrilling 3–2 win
articles.summary: Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer on target as Chelsea open scoring within 31 seconds of the match in London.
articles.body:
Chelsea began life under new coach Xabi Alonso with a breathless 3-2 Premier League victory at West London neighbours Fulham as their exciting front three of Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer all found the net.

Chelsea’s first league match of the season got off to a dream start on Monday when Palmer – looking back to his best after struggling with an injury last season – passed to Joao Pedro, and the Brazilian flicked the ball over goalkeeper Bernd Leno 31 seconds into the first half.

It was the quickest goal scored in the opening round of fixtures on Sunday in the Premier League’s 34-year history.

Fulham equalised when Josh King beat goalkeeper Robert Sanchez at his near post in the 24th minute, giving the home fans something to cheer against their fiercest rivals.

But two of Chelsea’s new signings then combined in the 41st as central defender Maxence Lacroix jinked down the right before cutting the ball back to the club’s 117 million pounds ($159.4m) record signing Rogers, who made no mistake.

Four minutes into the second half, Joao Pedro held up the ball in attack and fed Palmer, who angled a shot through Leno’s legs, underlining the midfielder’s return to form after missing out on a place with England at the World Cup.

“It was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard,” Palmer told Sky Sports.

“Obviously, with the injuries I’ve had to try and prevent them and work extra hard day in, day out. I know the talent I’ve got, so I can put in performances like that.”

Fulham’s Gonzalo Garcia, on his league debut after signing from Real Madrid, gave the hosts some hope by heading in after Sanchez could only parry a Timothy Castagne shot in the 54th.

Fulham then had a great chance to level again through Antonee Robinson in the 78th minute, but his chip over a stranded Sanchez went wide, and Chelsea held out to claim the points.

Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez — a linchpin of World Cup runners-up Argentina , who has been linked with a move to Manchester City — was greeted with loud boos from the home fans when he came on as a substitute midway through the second half.

Alonso’s win in his first competitive match since taking over at Stamford Bridge came at the expense of his former Liverpool and Spain teammate Alvaro Arbeloa — similarly making his Premier League debut as a coach — who also briefly succeeded Alonso as Real Madrid manager last season.

Alonso will hope midfielder Moises Caicedo and new fullback Marco Palestra, who are injured, will provide more solidity, while Sanchez could face an early challenge from Mike Penders, who has returned to Chelsea from sister club Racing Strasbourg.

articles.title: Federer to play tennis at US Open but rules out Williams-like return
articles.summary: The 20-time Grand Slam champion confirmed he’s only going to play in an exhibition match and has no plans to return.
articles.body:
Roger Federer is actually nervous about his tennis.

The man who won five straight US Open championships during the height of his dominance of the sport is set to play again in Arthur Ashe Stadium on Tuesday night for the first time since 2019. And he’s not quite sure how the game that perhaps nobody ever made look more elegant will appear now.

list 1 of 4 Gauff, Fils win Cincinnati tennis titles in run-up to US Open

list 2 of 4 Tennis: Philippines’ Eala wins first WTA title, Fritz claims DC crown

list 3 of 4 Venus Williams hits 13-game tennis losing streak with Cincinnati Open exit

list 4 of 4 Ceferin won’t challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency but tells him to quit

“I haven’t played a singles set in, I don’t know, [Hubert] Hurkacz at Wimbledon maybe, so it’s been five years,” Federer said on Monday, referring to his 2021 quarterfinal loss in his last Grand Slam match.

“I don’t know how it’s going to go tomorrow. So there is a lot of uncertainty but a lot of happiness that I can return to Arthur Ashe, a place where I have had so many beautiful moments.”

It’s only one set of singles in an exhibition against Andy Roddick and one set of doubles with John McEnroe against Roddick and Andre Agassi. The winner of 20 Grand Slam singles titles should be fine for those.

But a return to tennis beyond that, competing in major tennis tournaments in his mid-40s like Venus and Serena Williams?

“No, no, no, no. No, not at all,” Federer said during a news conference.

“Thanks for asking. I wasn’t sure if the question was going to get asked, but I’m happy you did so I can clarify in case anybody thought.”

At 45, Federer still looks fit, and said he enjoys working out in the gym. But he said he goes through long stretches where he is rarely on the court.

His lengthy absence from the US Open has done little to dampen his popularity, based on the number of people around the grounds who were mentioning his name. The appearance of “Roger Federer” up on the big board for all to see again, before his afternoon practice on Ashe, where Federer collected the trophy every year from 2004-08, was a welcome sight for his fans.

The trip to New York is a stop for Federer on his way to Newport, Rhode Island, where he will be enshrined in the International Tennis Hall of Fame on Saturday.

Federer never really had the chance to say goodbye to New York as a player, because there was no way to know his loss to Grigor Dimitrov in the 2019 quarterfinals would be his last match. He had reached the French Open semifinals and the Wimbledon final earlier that year, falling to Rafael Nadal in Paris and then Novak Djokovic in a fifth-set tiebreaker at the All England Club.

It was easy to imagine him returning to the US Open the next year and making another deep run. But after falling to Djokovic in the semifinals of the Australian Open to begin 2020, he had knee surgery that February, then another procedure in May.

He returned to play in the French Open in 2021 but had to withdraw before his fourth-round match. After the loss to Hurkacz – where he appeared to struggle and lost 6-0 in the third set – Federer had another knee surgery that August and knew there would be no more comebacks.

“The knee can’t do it any more. It’s tired,” he recalled thinking. “The mind can’t be patient even more and wait for another couple years and see what happens.”

Federer knows Tuesday night won’t be real tennis, joking that he and Roddick hopefully would be respectful and not try to drop shot each other. But it will be different from when he did return to Ashe a couple of years back to watch.

“They gave me an ovation because they saw me on the big screen, but I just feel, like, tomorrow and I guess today, as well, and Monday next week, it really gives me a true opportunity to say thank you and goodbye, which I think is important for some,” Federer said.

articles.title: Jai Arrow granted special dispensation to reach South Sydney Rabbitohs century after MND retirement
articles.summary: Jai Arrow, who retired in May following an MND diagnosis, will reach century of appearances for South Sydney Rabbitohs after NRL grant special dispensation for the 31-year-old to feature in Gold Coast Titans and South Sydney games
articles.body:
The NRL is planning an exception to its rules to allow Jai Arrow to reach the 100-game milestone for the South Sydney Rabbitohs after retiring earlier this year due to a motor neurone disease diagnosis.

MND Australia describes it as an umbrella term for a group of progressive neurological conditions in which the motor neurones degenerate. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is the most common form, and is often called Lou Gehrig's disease.

  • Jai Arrow retires at 30 after MND diagnosis
  • Motor Neurone Disease explained: What is it?
  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video

As part of an agreement with the Rabbitohs, the NRL granted South Sydney special dispensation to include Arrow, 31, as an extra player on Tuesday's official team list and an additional interchange in their rotation for Saturday's game against the Gold Coast Titans.

A similar dispensation will be granted for South Sydney's final regular-season game against the Sydney Roosters.

According to the NRL, Arrow will get dressed in South Sydney playing kit on both matchdays, join the Rabbitohs in the dressing room, lead the team onto the field, become the team's first interchange within seconds of the opening whistle without taking part in any play, and then remain on the interchange bench in his playing kit for the rest of the game.

It will take Arrow's tally to 180 career NRL games and 100 for the Rabbitohs, in addition to his representative appearances for Queensland in the annual State of Origin series.

Australian Rugby League Commission chairman Peter V'landys said it was a chance for the sport to be a "conduit to bring out the best of humanity".

"This thoughtful gesture by the South Sydney Rabbitohs shows the true heart of our game," V'landys said. "Jai has inspired millions of people around the world with the courage and strength he has shown in his fight with MND. He is not only a great player, but an extraordinary person.

"Reaching 100 games for the Rabbitohs is a special achievement, one that Jai, his family and everyone who has supported him should be incredibly proud of. The entire rugby league community stands with Jai and is honoured to celebrate this remarkable milestone with him."

Rugby league star Rob Burrow and Scotland rugby union great Doddie Weir are among the high-profile sportsmen to have died from the illness in recent years.
